chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you wish to know my companions, look at the one whose piety is most intense, who fears his Creator, and hopes for his Reward. And when you see these, then these are my companions.'
ai.seo_question: How to identify the true companions of the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the hallmark of his true companions (Ashab) is a triad of spiritual virtues: intense piety (wara'), awe of the Creator, and hopeful expectation of divine reward. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, underscores the Shia emphasis on inner moral integrity and God-consciousness (taqwa) as the primary markers of authentic religious adherence, distinguishing them from mere nominal followers.
